questions.question: What is the expected major product when D-Glucose is treated with Bromine water (Br2, H2O, pH 6)?
questions.explanation: Treating D-Glucose with Bromine water (Br2, H2O, pH 6) yields D-Gluconic acid (aldonic acid). Rationale: Mild bromine oxidation selectively oxidizes the aldehyde carbon (C1) to carboxylic acid without affecting primary alcohol.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of D-Glucose into D-Glucaric acid (aldaric acid)?
questions.explanation: To convert D-Glucose into D-Glucaric acid (aldaric acid), the appropriate reagent is Dilute nitric acid (HNO3) / heat. Rationale: Strong nitric acid oxidizes both the terminal aldehyde (C1) and primary alcohol (C6) into carboxylic acids.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when D-Glucose is treated with Sodium borohydride (NaBH4) in H2O?
questions.explanation: Treating D-Glucose with Sodium borohydride (NaBH4) in H2O yields D-Glucitol (D-sorbitol). Rationale: Hydride reduction of the carbonyl group converts open-chain aldose into the corresponding polyhydroxy alditol.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of D-Galactose into D-Galactonic acid + Metallic silver mirror (Ag(s))?
questions.explanation: To convert D-Galactose into D-Galactonic acid + Metallic silver mirror (Ag(s)), the appropriate reagent is Ag(NH3)2+ / aqueous OH-. Rationale: Reducing sugars with free hemiacetals reduce silver(I) diamine complex to elemental silver.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when D-Glucose is treated with Methanol (CH3OH) / dry HCl (g)?
questions.explanation: Treating D-Glucose with Methanol (CH3OH) / dry HCl (g) yields Methyl alpha-D-glucopyranoside + Methyl beta-D-glucopyranoside. Rationale: Acid-catalyzed condensation of anomeric hydroxyl with alcohol forms stable alpha and beta acetal glycosides.

questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of Methyl alpha-D-glucopyranoside into Methyl 2,3,4,6-tetra-O-methyl-alpha-D-glucopyranoside?
questions.explanation: To convert Methyl alpha-D-glucopyranoside into Methyl 2,3,4,6-tetra-O-methyl-alpha-D-glucopyranoside, the appropriate reagent is Excess iodomethane (CH3I) + Ag2O. Rationale: Williamson ether synthesis converts all free hydroxyl groups into methyl ethers.

questions.question: Which starting material will react with 1. HCN; 2. H2, Pd-BaSO4; 3. Aqueous H3O+ to yield D-Glucose + D-Mannose (diastereomeric aldohexose epimers) as the major product?
questions.explanation: D-Arabinose (aldopentose) reacts with 1. HCN; 2. H2, Pd-BaSO4; 3. Aqueous H3O+ to yield D-Glucose + D-Mannose (diastereomeric aldohexose epimers). Rationale: Cyanohydrin formation followed by reduction and hydrolysis adds one carbon to the carbonyl end.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when D-Glucose (aldohexose) is treated with 1. NH2OH; 2. Ac2O; 3. NaOCH3 in methanol?
questions.explanation: Treating D-Glucose (aldohexose) with 1. NH2OH; 2. Ac2O; 3. NaOCH3 in methanol yields D-Arabinose (aldopentose) + HCN. Rationale: Oxime formation, dehydration to cyanohydrin acetate, and basic loss of HCN shortens the aldose chain by 1 carbon.

questions.question: Which starting material will react with Sodium periodate (NaIO4) to yield Dialdehyde cleavage product + Formic acid as the major product?
questions.explanation: Methyl alpha-D-glucopyranoside reacts with Sodium periodate (NaIO4) to yield Dialdehyde cleavage product + Formic acid. Rationale: Periodic acid cleaves vicinal diol C-C bonds with oxidation to aldehydes.

questions.question: What is the expected major product when Sucrose (table sugar) is treated with Invertase (or aqueous H3O+)?
questions.explanation: Treating Sucrose (table sugar) with Invertase (or aqueous H3O+) yields D-Glucose + D-Fructose (invert sugar). Rationale: Hydrolysis of the alpha-1,beta-2-glycosidic bond cleaves disaccharide into glucose and fructose monosaccharides.
